```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
#install.packages("formattable")
library(formattable)
library(janitor)
```


#Bureau of Economic Research Local GDP data
```{r}
bea <- read_csv("./data/bea_md_gdp_county_2024_CAGDP91.csv", skip=3) |> 
  clean_names()
```


# Examine description.
Documentation

```{r}
bea_govt <- bea |> 
  filter(line_code %in% c(1, 2, 83)) |> 
  subset(select = -c(line_code)) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = description, values_from = x2024) |> 
  clean_names() |> 
  rename(government = government_and_government_enterprises, total = all_industry_total) |> 
  mutate(across(c(total, private_industries, government), as.numeric)) |> 
  mutate(geo_name = str_remove_all(geo_name, ", MD"))

```

#Totals, percentages
```{r}

bea_govt <- bea_govt |> 
  mutate(table_total = private_industries + government,
         diff = total - table_total,
         pct_gov = round(government/total*100))

```


# Plot the pct
```{r}
ggplot(bea_govt, aes(x = pct_gov, y = reorder(geo_name, pct_gov), fill = pct_gov)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Pct government in local Maryland counties",
    subtitle = "2024 BEA data",
    caption = "Graphic by Rob Wells, 10-26-2026",
    y = "county",
    x = "Pct govt of GDP"
  )

```

Adding labels, thanks Gemimi
```{r}
ggplot(bea_govt, aes(x = pct_gov, y = reorder(geo_name, pct_gov), fill = geo_name == "Maryland")) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  
  # Set colors: gold/yellow for Maryland (TRUE), grey for everything else (FALSE)
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#FFD700", "FALSE" = "grey75")) +
  
  # Add labels to the bars
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(round(pct_gov, 1), "%")),
    hjust = -0.2,
    size = 3.5,
    color = "grey20"
  ) +
  
  # Expand x-axis slightly so outside labels aren't cut off
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Pct government in local Maryland counties",
    subtitle = "2024 BEA data",
    caption = "Graphic by Rob Wells, 10-26-2026",
    y = "county",
    x = "Pct govt of GDP"
  )
```

#Simplify PG Data
```{r}

pg_places_brief <- pg |> 
   select(city_town,  income_per_capita, census_response_rate2020, census_response_rate2010, nbanks_zip, pct_anymembershp_zip, zip, tot_pop, age_above65, median_age, white, black, asian, geoid, tract,tract_name)
```

#Household income
```{r}
#PG Income
summary(pg$income_median)
  #  Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
  # 35313   58523   71963   79214   97970  152334 
#correct. but the data was compiled in a wonky way so this is a median of the medians of the census tracts, which is incorrect and doesn't reflect the actual county median of $101,798.
```

#Filter for both above-median census_response_rate2020 and Percent of membership in Civic Organization.

```{r}
# above <- pg |> 
#   filter(census_response_rate2020 >= 0.7190 & pct_anymembershp_zip >=  0.5037) |> 
#   arrange(desc(pct_anymembershp_zip))

above <- pg |> 
  filter(census_response_rate2020 > median(census_response_rate2020, na.rm = TRUE) & 
         pct_anymembershp_zip > median(pct_anymembershp_zip, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  arrange(desc(pct_anymembershp_zip))



summary(above$census_response_rate2020)
 #  Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
 # 0.7210  0.7535  0.8010  0.8027  0.8500  0.9000 

summary(above$pct_anymembershp_zip)
 #   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
 # 0.5058  0.5230  0.5475  0.5656  0.6007  0.6523
```

#Tracts with below median per capita income and higher than median participation
```{r}

low_and_active <- pg |> 
  filter(income_per_capita < 32613 & pct_anymembershp_zip >  0.5037) |> 
  arrange(desc(pct_anymembershp_zip))

write_csv(low_and_active, "./output/pg_co_low_income_active.csv")

```
